title: Solving Wordle using information theory
beats: Wordle as an excuse for information theory; build a bot; preview its play
Watch the bot guess, read grey/yellow/green feedback; solved in three
Real goal: explain information and entropy
First idea: common letters; friend's different opening; no way to score guesses
Define the game: ~13,000 allowed guesses, ~2,300 answers; why ignore the answer list
Concrete guess: a pattern leaves 58 words of ~13,000; rare means informative
Bar chart of probabilities over all 3^5 patterns; long tail
Puzzle: three words starting W, ending Y, containing R
One bit = halving possibilities; two bits = quarter; derive information from halvings
Why logs: easy numbers, and information adds where probabilities multiply
Expected information: weary 4.9 bits vs slate higher (about 5.8)
Entropy named after von Neumann joke; read it as expected information
Entropy as uniformity and as log of number of possibilities (16 patterns is 4 bits)
Bot picks guess with highest entropy; plays through a real game with margin annotations
Compare expected vs actual info; uncertainty bits equal log2 of remaining words
Quiz: what does one bit left mean? two candidates
Simulate all words with naive bot: average near 4; people do 3
Add word frequencies via sigmoid-shaped prior with cutoff
Entropy with 4 equal words is 2 bits; with 12 rare extra words only 2.11
Entropy used two ways: guess quality and remaining uncertainty
Score = P(win now) plus expected extra guesses estimated from past games vs uncertainty
Plot of guesses vs uncertainty, fit, new average about 3.6; second-best 3.43 with real list
Two-step lookahead possible; not enough time; can't average 3 anyway

theory: Information theory is taught by letting a single familiar game produce a stream of concrete numbers (58 of 13,000, 4.9 bits) and building each definition from the previous count: halving, then bits, then log, then expected value. Every new concept is immediately used in the bot, and the bot's failures (average 4, then 3.6) motivate each next refinement.
velocity: Scene builder: a persistent distribution bar chart where each pattern bar can be selected to show matching words.
Voice: derive a formula from two or three tabulated examples, then say the formula.
Orchestrator: run the 'metric vs outcome' validation loop as a standard beat.
Learner model: ask a prediction (word count left) before revealing each result.
Evals: confirm tutor states what is deliberately excluded and why.
Transcript caveat: stored transcript is Arabic machine translation; timestamps reliable, paraphrases approximate.
quote: think of entropy as the expected information value of a guess
